source: Blockstream public Esplora Bitcoin mainnet API, read-only GET
selection: At capture, select current reported tip minus six blocks; do not select by economic outcome or timestamp. One block only, no historical chain scan.
question: Can a raw mainnet block establish an independently timestamped, native-satoshi coinbase reward/fee-claim observation without relying on a retrospective daily aggregator?
mechanism_theory: Confirmed native BTC settlement fees could contain chain-demand information beyond market prices and venue trade-count composition; this does not identify miners selling BTC or predict returns without separate tests.
information_clock: Record UTC request and receipt around every public response. Header nTime, median-time-past, provider Date, and receipt are different clocks. A historic block fetched now was only observed by this process now.
minimal_checks: One tip-minus-six block: hash/header, best-chain status, coinbase transaction and hex, inclusion proof, all output values in integer satoshis, and height-based subsidy. Reject proof failures or clock inconsistencies.
boundary: Coinbase payout minus allowed subsidy is at most a fee-claim proxy; if miners underclaim, it differs from total block transaction fees. One block is not a completed day, a historical receipt, or enough independent outcomes for an alpha screen.
economics_gate: Only if source scope, timestamp and pre-decision receipt are qualified across at least ten non-overlapping events with early/late support should one fixed fee-information hypothesis and matched exposure/cost/start-time account test be registered. No old CoinMetrics values may be backfilled as receipts.
